title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
summary:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.
Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.
Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.
With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.
The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place.

title: Failed asylum seekers face removal without five-day notice period
summary:
The government is to change the law so that it no longer has to give failed asylum seekers notice before they are removed from the country.
Currently, people are given five working days' notice but ministers believe this leads to last-minute appeals which delay the process.
The move was criticised by the Refugee Council which said: "Removing people at such short notice will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety to people."
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood will make the change by amending the Immigration and Asylum Bill which is currently going through Parliament.
The amendment will scrap the notice requirement for those who have exhausted the asylum appeals process.

title: Record number of migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands
summary:
New European Union migration and asylum laws have largely failed to stem the flow of migrants to Spain and its territories.
Spain’s Maritime Rescue Service said it had rescued 1,488 migrants aboard 14 dinghies, also known as pirogues, most of whom arrived on El Hierro in the Canary Islands from West Africa on Saturday.
Spain’s Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres is visiting ⁠El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals.
Al Jazeera’s Bernard Smith, reporting from El Hierro, said the arrival this year has set a record in the 32 years since statistics have been collected.
Most of the migrants arriving in El Hierro depart from West Africa, many leaving from Senegal, with hopes of reaching mainland Europe.

title: Five EU countries announce plan to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
summary:
In a joint statement, 47 aid, trade union and rights groups urged ‌the five countries to ​abandon the Rwanda plan.
Five European countries have announced a plan to send rejected asylum seekers to a processing centre in Rwanda as early as next year, drawing condemnation from rights groups who said it would leave vulnerable people at risk of abuse.
Human rights groups criticised the plans, saying that EU countries could not guarantee their rights would be respected there.
In a joint statement, 47 aid, trade union and rights groups urged ‌the five countries to abandon the Rwanda plan — echoing criticisms of a different migration settlement plan between Britain and Rwanda in the early 2020s.
A Human Rights Watch researcher said the deal “would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad”.

summary:

title: Canary Islands migrant arrivals hit record high
summary:
Another 1,261 migrants reached El Hierro on Sunday, bringing the three-day total across the archipelago to 3,684, according to Spanish news agency EFE.
The migrants arrived in the Canary Islands aboard 15 boats on Saturday, including 173 minors among the passengers, EFE reported, citing provisional figures from rescue services.
Canary Islands President Fernando Clavijo accused the central government of failing to act quickly enough, demanding the immediate implementation of promised emergency measures.
The government has also committed over €16 million ($17.6 million) in emergency aid.
The record arrivals come despite the EU’s efforts to curb irregular migration through tighter border controls and agreements with African countries.

title: EU capitals to unveil deal to start sending rejected migrants to Rwanda, raising fresh questions over Labour's move to ditch the Tories' flagship deportation scheme to stop the boats
summary:
Several EU capitals will today announce a deal to start sending rejected migrants to Rwanda, raising fresh questions about why Labour ditched the Tories' flagship deportation scheme.
Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands are set to unveil the deal – aimed at reducing illegal land border and Mediterranean boat crossings – following months of talks.
A deportation hub created in Rwanda would function as a pilot project and deals with other non-EU countries – and involving other EU nations – are set to follow.
'The most obvious failing was Labour scrapping the Rwanda partnership – a scheme now being taken up by so many other countries the Government professes to admire.'
Tomorrow's deal would only apply to asylum seekers who had exhausted all of their options for securing legal residence in the EU and were rejected.

title: £80,000 a day is spent ferrying small boat migrants around: Labour's staggering splurge on taxis and shuttle buses
summary:
Labour has been splurging nearly £80,000 a day on 'chauffeuring' small-boat migrants around in taxis and shuttle buses.
The staggering sum includes ferrying asylum seekers in taxis to medical appointments – such as to a GP or dental practice – and laying on minibuses for days out.
He added: 'Taxpayers should not be shelling out so asylum seekers can be chauffeured around.
Earlier this year an investigation found taxis were being used to pick up migrants from asylum hotels to take them to medical appointments.
'We are reducing reliance on expensive asylum hotels and transport by using options that deliver better value for the taxpayer.'
